# Auth Barrier Checklist: P-RF03 — Biometric authentication vault

**Purpose**: Validate requirements quality for the three dimensions where this unit carries the most risk — the on-device security boundary (FR-002/FR-014/FR-015), lifecycle/timing of the lock (FR-001/FR-007–FR-010), and failure/fallback paths (FR-004/FR-006/FR-012, Edge Cases) — before `/speckit-tasks` turns spec.md into implementation work.
**Created**: 2026-10-11
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Security & On-Device Boundary

- [ ] CHK001 Is "entirely on-device" for authentication (FR-002) specific enough to rule out any transient transmission of the PIN value or raw biometric data, even for logging/telemetry purposes? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK002 Does the spec define what "the single typed-failure network call path already established by the foundation unit" (FR-014) means precisely enough that it cannot be read as permitting a new ad hoc HTTP call? [Clarity, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK003 Is it specified that passing the local barrier must never be treated as equivalent to backend authentication (FR-015) in every call site that checks "is the user authenticated"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK004 Are the storage requirements for the Device PIN specified in a way that is testable for requirements quality purposes — e.g., "never transmitted to or validated by the backend" (Key Entities) — without mandating a specific hashing/storage mechanism that belongs in plan.md rather than spec.md? [Consistency, Spec §Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK005 Is there a requirement covering what happens if the device's secure storage for the PIN becomes unavailable or is cleared by the OS between sessions (distinct from "no PIN configured yet")? [Gap, Coverage]
- [ ] CHK006 Does the spec distinguish, for requirements purposes, between "biometrics preference" (an account flag written via the backend) and "the actual biometric check" (never backend-validated) clearly enough that a reader could not conflate the two? [Clarity, Spec §Key Entities]

## Lifecycle & Timing

- [ ] CHK007 Is the 5-minute background threshold specified with an unambiguous reference point (e.g., time of backgrounding vs. time of last unlock) so two readers could not compute different results from the same scenario? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-007, §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK008 Is "resume exactly the screen and state the user left" (FR-008) defined with enough specificity to be objectively verified (e.g., does "state" include scroll position, in-progress text input, modal visibility)? [Measurability, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK009 Is the requirement that the barrier appears "before the previously visible screen becomes visible or interactive" (FR-007) clear about whether the underlying screen may render behind the barrier (visually present but not interactive) or must not render at all? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK010 Does the spec define behavior for the boundary condition where the app is backgrounded multiple times within the 5-minute window (e.g., does each backgrounding reset the timer, or only the first)? [Gap, Edge Case]
- [ ] CHK011 Is the distinction between "app suspended in background" and "app process killed by the OS" (Edge Cases) specified with criteria an implementer could use to classify a given resume event, or does it assume platform-reported state the spec doesn't name? [Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK012 Is FR-009's "fixed value with no user-facing setting" requirement consistent with there being no other requirement or assumption elsewhere in the spec that implies configurability (e.g., via a future Settings screen)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009, §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK013 Does the spec specify what happens to Vault Lock State (and the last-unlocked timestamp) across an app restart that is not itself a biometric/PIN prompt event (e.g., a crash-and-relaunch under 5 minutes)? [Gap, Edge Case]

## Failure & Fallback Paths

- [ ] CHK014 Is "a biometric attempt fails or is not recognized" (FR-004) specified broadly enough to clearly cover user-cancellation and OS-level dismissal as the same case as sensor misread, or does it leave room for a narrower reading that treats them differently? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK015 Is the "no limit that locks them out of the app entirely" requirement (User Story 2, Acceptance Scenario 3) reconciled with any implicit expectation of rate-limiting or lockout behavior that might be assumed from typical PIN-entry UX, so there's no conflict for an implementer to resolve on their own? [Consistency, Spec §User Story 2]
- [ ] CHK016 Does the spec define what, if anything, is logged or surfaced when repeated incorrect PIN attempts occur (e.g., is there a requirement for a soft warning before "usar e-mail e senha" is suggested more prominently), or is zero such behavior an explicit scope decision? [Gap, Assumption]
- [ ] CHK017 Is the exact error message text ("Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN", FR-004) specified as a requirement in a way consistent with how other user-facing strings are specified elsewhere in the spec (e.g., PIN mismatch message in FR-012 has no literal text given)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK018 Is the fallback for "no biometric hardware or nothing enrolled at the OS level" (Edge Cases) specified identically for first-launch-ever-on-device vs. a device that previously had biometrics enabled and lost enrollment, or could these require different requirements that the spec doesn't separate? [Coverage, Edge Case]
- [ ] CHK019 Does the spec specify what the PIN entry screen shows immediately after the biometric prompt is dismissed/cancelled by the user (distinct from a failed scan) — is this covered by FR-004 or left ambiguous? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK020 Is the "usar e-mail e senha" escape hatch (FR-006) specified as available from every state of the vault screen (biometric prompt, PIN-after-failure, first-time PIN setup) or only from some, and if only some, is that scoping explicit? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006]

## First-Time PIN Setup Interplay

- [ ] CHK021 Is the requirement that an app kill mid-setup "resumes the PIN setup flow" (Edge Cases) specific enough about what state is resumed from (e.g., back to PIN entry step 1, or preserving the first-entered PIN for confirmation) to be implementable without guessing? [Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK022 Does the spec reconcile FR-013's "optionally enable Face ID/Touch ID... as part of first-time PIN setup" with the Clarifications answer that the `PATCH /account/settings` write is fire-and-forget — i.e., is it clear the user's biometric toggle takes effect locally regardless of that write's outcome? [Consistency, Spec §FR-013, §FR-014, §Clarifications]
- [ ] CHK023 Is there a requirement for what the user sees (if anything) when the fire-and-forget `biometricEnabled` write fails, or is "no synchronous retry, no blocking" (FR-014) explicitly understood to also mean no error UI at all? [Gap, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-014]

## Measurability & Traceability

- [ ] CHK024 Can SC-001's "100% of cold launches and background resumes... show the authentication barrier" be objectively measured given the requirements as written, or does it depend on an undefined instrumentation/observation method? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK025 Can SC-005's "screen state underneath... is unchanged in every observed case" be verified against a concrete, enumerated definition of "state" (scroll position, visible content) or does it rely on an open-ended notion of equivalence? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK026 Is a requirement & acceptance-criteria ID scheme established and consistently applied (FR-001…FR-018, SC-001…SC-005) such that every acceptance scenario can be traced to at least one FR? [Traceability]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK027 Is the assumption that "device biometric availability... is read from the platform's own biometrics API" (Assumptions) validated against FR-003's requirement to attempt biometrics first when available — i.e., is there a requirement for what happens if that platform API itself errors rather than returning a clean available/unavailable answer? [Gap, Assumption]
- [ ] CHK028 Is the dependency on F000's session machinery (FR-015, "silent renewal, or a full login if the session can no longer be renewed") specified with enough detail that a reader can tell which F000 component owns that decision, without this spec needing to redefine it? [Dependency, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK029 Is the assumption that the "Sessão expirada" overlay is "unaffected by this unit" (Assumptions) consistent with FR-001's requirement that the vault MUST gate every cold launch/resume — i.e., is there a documented reason the two don't collide when a session expires while the vault is also due to trigger? [Conflict, Consistency, Spec §Assumptions, §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK030 Is the assumption that no separate PIN-creation screen exists in the prototype, and that the same keypad component is reused for create-then-confirm (Assumptions), reconciled with FR-005's requirement describing PIN entry generically — does FR-005 as written clearly apply to both unlock-entry and setup-entry, or only to one? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005, §Assumptions]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference

104	- [ ] T032 [US1] Write `VaultBloc` tests in `test/features/vault/presentation/bloc/vault_bloc_test.dart` (`bloc_test`) for `VaultOpened` → `unlockBiometricFirst` → biometric `success` → unlocked — depends on T027
105	- [ ] T033 [US1] Write a widget test for `VaultLifecycleObserver` in `test/features/vault/presentation/widgets/vault_lifecycle_observer_test.dart`, driving `AppLifecycleState.paused`/`.resumed` via `tester.binding.handleAppLifecycleStateChanged(...)` (contracts/vault-lifecycle.md), asserting a relock push occurs at a ≥5-minute gap with `lastUnlockedAt != null`, and no push occurs under 5 minutes or when `lastUnlockedAt == null` — depends on T029

111	## Phase 4: User Story 2 - Biometric failure falls back to PIN (Priority: P1)
112	
113	**Goal**: A failed, cancelled, or unrecognized biometric attempt immediately offers PIN entry with
114	the exact fallback message, never locking the user out; a correct PIN still unlocks.
115	
116	**Independent Test**: Force a biometric failure; confirm the PIN screen appears with the error
117	message, then confirm a correct PIN still unlocks the app.
118	
119	### Tests for User Story 2
120	
121	- [ ] T034 [P] [US2] Write `VerifyPinUseCase` tests in `test/features/vault/domain/usecases/verify_pin_usecase_test.dart` against a fake `VaultRepository`: correct PIN → `true`; incorrect PIN → `false`
122	
123	### Implementation for User Story 2
124	
125	- [ ] T035 [P] [US2] Create `VerifyPinUseCase` in `lib/features/vault/domain/usecases/verify_pin_usecase.dart` — thin delegation to `repo.verifyPin(pin)`
126	- [ ] T036 [US2] In `VaultBloc`, handle `attemptBiometricAuth()` outcomes `failed`/`cancelled`/`notAvailable` (all three routed identically per contracts/vault-repository.md: FR-004 doesn't distinguish "not recognized" from "user tapped away" from "biometrics became unavailable mid-attempt") by emitting the PIN-entry state with the error banner text "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN" (FR-004); handle `PinDigitEntered`/`PinBackspacePressed`/`PinSubmitted` via `VerifyPinUseCase`; on a correct PIN, call `repo.markUnlocked(DateTime.now())` and emit the unlocked state (data-model.md State transitions: "correct PIN → markUnlocked() → context.go(AppRoutes.home)") — this is the only unlock path for a user whose biometric preference is off, so skipping it here leaves `lastUnlockedAt` null and silently defeats `VaultLifecycleObserver`'s relock guard (contracts/vault-lifecycle.md) for every PIN-only user; on an incorrect PIN, clear the entered digits and keep the error state with no attempt limit (Edge Cases: "never produce a hard lockout") — depends on T021, T035
127	- [ ] T037 [US2] In `VaultPage`, build the PIN-entry UI state using the shared `PinKeypad` (lib/features/vault/presentation/widgets/pin_keypad.dart): 4-digit progress dots, the biometric-failure error banner when present, digits cleared and redisplayed empty after an incorrect submission — depends on T022, T023, T036
128	- [ ] T038 [US2] Extend `VaultBloc` tests in `test/features/vault/presentation/bloc/vault_bloc_test.dart`: biometric `failed`/`cancelled`/`notAvailable` → PIN-entry state with the exact error message; correct PIN → unlocked AND `repo.markUnlocked` was called (verify via the fake/mock `VaultRepository`); incorrect PIN → digits cleared, error state retained, a second correct attempt afterward still succeeds (no lockout) — depends on T036
129

132	---

134	## Phase 5: User Story 3 - Setting up the PIN for the first time (Priority: P2)
135	
136	**Goal**: The very first successful login/sign-up on a device with no PIN leads straight into
137	create-then-confirm PIN setup, with an optional biometrics opt-in, before Home/Chat is reachable; a
138	mismatched confirmation is rejected without saving; a mid-setup kill resumes setup on relaunch.
139	
140	**Independent Test**: Sign up fresh on a device with no PIN configured; confirm the create-PIN
141	screen appears before Home/Chat; a matching confirmation proceeds, a mismatched one does not.
142	
143	### Tests for User Story 3
144	
145	- [ ] T039 [P] [US3] Write `SavePinUseCase` tests in `test/features/vault/domain/usecases/save_pin_usecase_test.dart` against a fake `VaultRepository`, verifying it delegates to `repo.savePin(pin)`
146	- [ ] T040 [P] [US3] Write `SaveBiometricsPreferenceUseCase` tests in `test/features/vault/domain/usecases/save_biometrics_preference_usecase_test.dart` against fake `VaultRepository`/`BiometricsPreferenceRepository`: the local mirror is written synchronously *before* the network call fires (research.md R6); a `Left` result from `BiometricsPreferenceRepository.save` is discarded and does not throw or propagate — the usecase always completes
147	
148	### Implementation for User Story 3
149	
150	- [ ] T041 [P] [US3] Create `SavePinUseCase` in `lib/features/vault/domain/usecases/save_pin_usecase.dart` — thin delegation to `repo.savePin(pin)`; the 4-digit value it's given must already satisfy "exactly 4 digits, each `0`–`9`" (data-model.md Device PIN validation rule) — the bloc enforces this before calling, this usecase does not re-validate
151	- [ ] T042 [US3] Create `SaveBiometricsPreferenceUseCase` in `lib/features/vault/domain/usecases/save_biometrics_preference_usecase.dart` implementing exactly the 3-step write path from data-model.md Biometrics Preference: (1) `repo.setBiometricPreferenceLocally(enabled)` synchronously; (2) `await biometricsPreferenceRepository.save(enabled)`, discarding the `Either<Failure, T>` result either way; (3) return/complete regardless of step 2's outcome (FR-014, Clarifications: "proceed locally and retry in the background") — depends on T006, T007
152	- [ ] T043 [US3] In `VaultBloc`, handle `pinSetupRequired` entry: create-PIN step holds the first 4-digit entry only in bloc memory (never written to storage yet — data-model.md); confirm step does a pure string-equality check — on match, call `SavePinUseCase` then, if `checkBiometricCapability() == available`, emit a biometric opt-in step, else proceed directly to the complete/unlocked transition (same transition T044 reaches after an opt-in choice — call `repo.markUnlocked(DateTime.now())` then emit the unlocked state); on mismatch, emit a clear mismatch message and return to the create-PIN step with nothing saved (FR-012) — depends on T021, T041, T042
153	- [ ] T044 [US3] In `VaultBloc`, handle `BiometricOptInToggled` by calling `SaveBiometricsPreferenceUseCase`, then call `repo.markUnlocked(DateTime.now())` and transition to the unlocked/complete state regardless of `SaveBiometricsPreferenceUseCase`'s outcome, proceeding to Home/Chat (FR-013, FR-014) — the `markUnlocked()` call here (and in T043's no-biometric-available branch) is required so `VaultLifecycleObserver`'s `repo.lastUnlockedAt != null` guard (contracts/vault-lifecycle.md) is already satisfied the first time a new user backgrounds the app after setup; without it, FR-007/SC-001 silently never trigger for a brand-new device's first background/resume cycle — depends on T043
154	- [ ] T045 [US3] Build the PIN-setup UI states in `VaultPage` — create-PIN step, confirm-PIN step with mismatch message, and (when biometric capability is available) the biometrics opt-in prompt — reusing the shared `PinKeypad`; on gatekeeper-mode completion, `context.go(AppRoutes.home)` — depends on T022, T023, T044
155	- [ ] T046 [US3] In `lib/features/auth/presentation/pages/login_signup_page.dart`, change the non-reauth `AuthStatus.authenticated` branch from `context.push(AppRoutes.home)` to `context.push(AppRoutes.vault)` — depends on T024
156	- [ ] T047 [US3] Extend `VaultBloc` tests in `test/features/vault/presentation/bloc/vault_bloc_test.dart`: `pinSetupRequired` → matching create/confirm → PIN saved, biometric opt-in available → `SaveBiometricsPreferenceUseCase` invoked → unlocked/complete AND `repo.markUnlocked` was called; matching create/confirm with no biometric capability available → skips the opt-in step → unlocked/complete AND `repo.markUnlocked` was called (T043's else-branch); mismatched confirm → mismatch message, create step re-entered, `savePin` never called; a `pinSetupRequired` re-open before confirmation completes (process killed mid-setup) re-enters the create step rather than any unlocked/Home state, since `hasPinConfigured()` is still `false` (Edge Cases) — depends on T043, T044
157	
158	**Checkpoint**: All of Stories 1–3 are independently functional — the full vault core loop (setup → unlock → fallback) works end to end.
159	
160	---
161	
162	## Phase 6: User Story 4 - Recovering access via full login (Priority: P3)
163	
164	**Goal**: A visible "usar e-mail e senha" link on the vault screen leads to the existing
165	email/password login, regardless of whether the vault is showing the biometric or PIN state.
166	
167	**Independent Test**: Tap "usar e-mail e senha" from the vault screen; confirm it leads to the
168	existing login screen; submitting valid credentials proceeds into the app.
169	
170	### Implementation for User Story 4
171	
172	- [ ] T048 [US4] Add a visible "usar e-mail e senha" text link to both the biometric-prompting and PIN-entry UI states in `VaultPage`, dispatching `UseEmailPasswordRequested` (FR-006) — depends on T028, T037
173	- [ ] T049 [US4] In `VaultBloc`, handle `UseEmailPasswordRequested` by triggering `context.push(AppRoutes.login)` from `VaultPage` (no bloc state change needed beyond the navigation side effect) — depends on T048
174	- [ ] T050 [US4] Write a widget test in `test/features/vault/presentation/pages/vault_page_test.dart` confirming the "usar e-mail e senha" link is present and triggers a push to `AppRoutes.login` from both the biometric-prompting and PIN-entry states — depends on T049
175	
176	**Checkpoint**: All four user stories are independently functional.
177	
178	---
179	
180	## Phase 7: Polish & Cross-Cutting Concerns
181	
182	**Purpose**: The constitution/quickstart gates that span every story above.
183	
184	- [ ] T051 [P] Run `fvm flutter analyze` and resolve any `always_use_package_imports`/lint findings under `lib/features/vault/`
185	- [ ] T052 [P] Run `test/architecture/domain_purity_test.dart` and confirm it still reports 0 violations with `lib/features/vault/domain/` included (RNF06)
186	- [ ] T053 Run `fvm flutter test --coverage`, extract `lib/**/domain/**` via `lcov --extract coverage/lcov.info 'lib/**/domain/**' -o coverage/domain.info`, and confirm ≥80% coverage with `lib/features/vault/domain/` included (RNF07)
187	- [ ] T054 Execute quickstart.md's manual verification on the iOS Simulator for Stories 1–4 and its edge cases: no-hardware/not-enrolled/OS-disabled-between-sessions shows PIN directly with no error; the exact 5-minute boundary; app killed mid-setup resumes setup; app killed while backgrounded is treated as cold launch; offline during the biometrics-preference write still completes setup and reaches Home/Chat
188	
189	---
190	
191	## Dependencies & Execution Order
192	
193	### Phase Dependencies
194	
195	- **Setup (Phase 1)**: No dependencies — start immediately.
196	- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: Depends on Setup (T003 for the route constant) — BLOCKS all user stories.
197	- **User Stories (Phase 3–6)**: All depend on Foundational completion.
198	  - US1 and US2 (both P1) should be done first — US2's "biometric fails → PIN" handler extends the
199	    same `VaultBloc` branch US1's biometric-success handler lives in (T027/T036 both touch
200	    `vault_bloc.dart`), so doing them in sequence avoids rework, even though each is independently
201	    testable once done.
202	  - US3 (P2) extends the same bloc/page with the `pinSetupRequired` branch — independent of US1/US2's
203	    code paths (different `VaultEntryMode` branch) but shares the file.
204	  - US4 (P3) only adds a link + navigation handler on top of UI states US1/US2 already built (T028, T037).
205	- **Polish (Phase 7)**: Depends on all four stories being complete.
206	
207	### Within Each User Story
208	
209	- Tests before/alongside implementation (written to fail first, per the template's convention).
210	- Domain usecases before bloc wiring; bloc wiring before the page UI that reads it.
211	- Story complete (bloc + page + test) before moving to the next priority.
212	
213	### Parallel Opportunities
214	
215	- T002, T003 (Setup) in parallel.
216	- T004, T005 (entities), T010 (design token), T007 (second repository interface) in parallel within Foundational.
217	- T009, T014, T017 (test files) can be written in parallel with each other once their respective implementation task lands.
218	- T025/T026 (US1 usecase + its test) in parallel with T034/T035 (US2 usecase + its test) — different files, both depend only on Foundational.
219	- T039/T040/T041 (US3 usecases + tests) in parallel with each other.
220	
221	---
222	
223	## Parallel Example: Foundational Phase
224	
225	```bash
226	# Launch independent entity/token files together:
227	Task: "Create VaultEntryMode enum in lib/features/vault/domain/entities/vault_entry_mode.dart"
228	Task: "Create BiometricCapability enum in lib/features/vault/domain/entities/biometric_capability.dart"
229	Task: "Add sizeKeypadTapTarget token to lib/core/design_tokens.dart"
230	Task: "Create BiometricsPreferenceRepository interface in lib/features/vault/domain/repositories/biometrics_preference_repository.dart"
231	```
232	
233	## Parallel Example: User Story 1 vs. User Story 2 usecases
234	
235	```bash
236	Task: "Create EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase in lib/features/vault/domain/usecases/evaluate_background_resume_usecase.dart"
237	Task: "Write EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase tests in test/features/vault/domain/usecases/evaluate_background_resume_usecase_test.dart"
238	Task: "Create VerifyPinUseCase in lib/features/vault/domain/usecases/verify_pin_usecase.dart"
239	Task: "Write VerifyPinUseCase tests in test/features/vault/domain/usecases/verify_pin_usecase_test.dart"
240	```
241	
242	---
243	
244	## Implementation Strategy
245	
246	### MVP First (User Story 1 Only)
247	
248	1. Complete Phase 1: Setup.
249	2. Complete Phase 2: Foundational (CRITICAL — blocks all stories).
250	3. Complete Phase 3: User Story 1.
251	4. **STOP and VALIDATE**: cold launch shows the biometric prompt before data; a successful scan
252	   proceeds; background ≥5 min re-prompts; background <5 min does not. Note that without User
253	   Story 3, this MVP slice has no PIN ever configured on a fresh device — validate it on a device
254	   where a PIN already exists (or treat US1+US3 as the realistic minimum demoable slice).
255	
256	### Incremental Delivery
257	
258	1. Setup + Foundational → foundation ready (vault route exists, resolves to an empty page).
259	2. Add US1 → biometric gate works (needs a pre-existing PIN to reach `unlockBiometricFirst`).
260	3. Add US2 → a failed scan no longer strands the user.
261	4. Add US3 → a fresh device can actually reach the vault for the first time (PIN now gets created) — this closes the loop US1/US2 needed a PIN for.
262	5. Add US4 → the "usar e-mail e senha" safety valve.
263	6. Polish → RNF06/07 gates + quickstart's full manual pass.
264	
265	Note the real dependency the priorities don't show on their own: **US3 produces the PIN that US1
266	and US2 require to exist.** Implementing in spec order (US1 → US2 → US3 → US4) is fine for
267	*writing* the code (Foundational already stubs `hasPinConfigured()`), but *manually demoing* US1/US2
268	end-to-end needs either a PIN seeded directly via `VaultRepository` in a test, or US3 done first.
269	
270	---
271	
272	## Notes
273	
274	- `vault_bloc.dart`, `vault_event.dart`, `vault_state.dart`, and `vault_page.dart` are each touched
275	  by multiple story phases (T021/T027/T036/T043/T044 for the bloc; T022/T028/T037/T045/T048 for the
276	  page) — this is the deliberate single-screen/single-bloc shape research.md R4 chose, not a
277	  same-file conflict to avoid.
278	- Every repository method this unit adds that is *not* network-backed (`VaultRepository`'s methods)
279	  intentionally returns plain types, not `Either<Failure, T>` — research.md R5. Only
280	  `BiometricsPreferenceRepository.save` does, and only its 3 failure-scenario tests (T017) count
281	  toward RNF09's 15/15.
282	- No task in this list touches `docs/input/`, `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, `.env`, or
283	  `lib/features/session/presentation/widgets/session_expired_overlay.dart` — all three are
284	  explicitly out of scope (FR-018, spec.md Assumptions).

# Tasks: P-RF03 — Biometric authentication vault

**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/`

**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/, quickstart.md (all present)

**Tests**: Included. plan.md's Testing section and quickstart.md's "Automated checks" explicitly name
the domain tests this unit's RNF07 coverage gate depends on (`EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase`,
`DetermineVaultEntryUseCase`, `VerifyPinUseCase`/`SavePinUseCase`, `BiometricsPreferenceRepositoryImpl`'s
3 failure scenarios), so test tasks are generated alongside implementation, `bloc_test`/`mocktail`
style, matching F000's existing test files exactly.

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story (US1–US4, spec.md priorities P1/P1/P2/P3). Per
research.md R4, all four stories share one route/page/bloc (`AppRoutes.vault` / `VaultPage` /
`VaultBloc`) by deliberate design — "independent" here means each story's acceptance scenarios can
be exercised and automated-tested on their own once Foundational is done, not that each story gets
its own screen.

## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`

- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependencies on an incomplete task)
- **[Story]**: US1 (biometric unlock), US2 (biometric-failure → PIN fallback), US3 (first-time PIN
  setup), US4 (recover via full login)

## Path Conventions

Single Flutter project (F000's existing `lib/`, `test/`) — see plan.md Project Structure. All new
files live under `lib/features/vault/` and `test/features/vault/`; four files touch existing F000
code at documented one-line extension points.

---

## Phase 1: Setup

**Purpose**: Dependencies and the one new route constant every later task needs.

- [ ] T001 Add `local_auth` and `crypto` to `pubspec.yaml` dependencies (research.md R1, R2), then run `fvm flutter pub get`
- [ ] T002 [P] Add `NSFaceIDUsageDescription` (a one-line usage string) to `ios/Runner/Info.plist` — required before any `local_auth` call, including a check, can be made on-device or in the Simulator (research.md R1)
- [ ] T003 [P] Add `static const String vault = '/vault';` to `AppRoutes` in `lib/core/routing/app_routes.dart`

---

## Phase 2: Foundational (Blocking Prerequisites)

**Purpose**: The shared repository/usecase/bloc/page plumbing every one of the four user stories
reads or extends. No story's acceptance scenario can be exercised, manually or in a test, until
this phase is done.

**⚠️ CRITICAL**: No user story work can begin until this phase is complete.

- [ ] T004 [P] Create `VaultEntryMode` enum (`pinSetupRequired`, `unlockBiometricFirst`, `unlockPinOnly`) in `lib/features/vault/domain/entities/vault_entry_mode.dart` (data-model.md Vault Lock State)
- [ ] T005 [P] Create `BiometricCapability` enum (`available`, `noHardware`, `notEnrolled`, `osDisabled`) in `lib/features/vault/domain/entities/biometric_capability.dart` (data-model.md Biometric Capability)
- [ ] T006 Create `VaultRepository` abstract interface in `lib/features/vault/domain/repositories/vault_repository.dart` — the exact method set from contracts/vault-repository.md (`hasPinConfigured`, `savePin`, `verifyPin`, `checkBiometricCapability`, `attemptBiometricAuth`, `isBiometricPreferenceEnabled`, `setBiometricPreferenceLocally`, `recordBackgrounded`, `consumeBackgroundedAt`, `markUnlocked`, `lastUnlockedAt`), including the `BiometricAuthOutcome` enum (`success`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `notAvailable`) it returns; no `local_auth` or `flutter_secure_storage` type may appear in this file (RNF06) — depends on T004, T005
- [ ] T007 [P] Create `BiometricsPreferenceRepository` abstract interface in `lib/features/vault/domain/repositories/biometrics_preference_repository.dart` — single method `Future<Either<Failure, void>> save(bool enabled)` (contracts/biometrics-preference-repository.md)
- [ ] T008 Create `DetermineVaultEntryUseCase` in `lib/features/vault/domain/usecases/determine_vault_entry_usecase.dart`, implementing exactly the branching in contracts/vault-repository.md (`!hasPinConfigured()` → `pinSetupRequired`; else `capability == available && preferred` → `unlockBiometricFirst`; else `unlockPinOnly`) — depends on T006
- [ ] T009 [P] Write `DetermineVaultEntryUseCase` tests in `test/features/vault/domain/usecases/determine_vault_entry_usecase_test.dart` against a fake `VaultRepository`, covering all four input combinations per quickstart.md: no PIN; PIN + biometric available + preferred; PIN + biometric available + not preferred; PIN + biometric unavailable — depends on T008
- [ ] T010 [P] Add `sizeKeypadTapTarget` token (value `72`, a `double`, dp) to `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` — the circular tap target for each of the keypad's 12 keys, per research.md R7; no other value this unit needs is new
- [ ] T011 Create `VaultSecureStorage` in `lib/features/vault/data/vault_secure_storage.dart` — Keychain-backed via `flutter_secure_storage`, two keys: PIN hash and local biometrics-preference mirror. `savePin`/PIN comparison MUST store and compare only `sha256(pin)` (hex string), never the raw digit string (research.md R2); the PIN value accepted MUST be "exactly 4 digits, each `0`–`9`, no partial/shorter value ever written or compared" (data-model.md Device PIN validation rule) — validate this shape before hashing
- [ ] T012 [P] Create `LocalAuthBiometricDataSource` in `lib/features/vault/data/local_auth_biometric_data_source.dart` — thin wrapper over `local_auth`'s `LocalAuthentication`, calling `authenticate(biometricOnly: true)` (research.md R1); the only file in this unit allowed to import `local_auth` types
- [ ] T013 Create `VaultRepositoryImpl` implementing `VaultRepository` in `lib/features/vault/data/vault_repository_impl.dart` — maps `LocalAuthBiometricDataSource`/`local_auth` results into `BiometricCapability`/`BiometricAuthOutcome` before returning (RNF06); `lastUnlockedAt`/`backgroundedAt` held in-memory only, never persisted (data-model.md Vault Lock State) — depends on T006, T011, T012
- [ ] T014 [P] Write `VaultRepositoryImpl` tests in `test/features/vault/data/vault_repository_impl_test.dart` (mocktail, mocking `VaultSecureStorage`/`LocalAuthBiometricDataSource`) covering: PIN hash round-trip (`savePin` then `verifyPin` with the same/different 4-digit value), each `BiometricCapability` mapping, `recordBackgrounded`/`consumeBackgroundedAt` clearing semantics (one resume evaluates the gap only once), `markUnlocked`/`lastUnlockedAt` — depends on T013
- [ ] T015 Create `BiometricsPreferenceRemoteDataSource` in `lib/features/vault/data/account/biometrics_preference_remote_data_source.dart` — `update({required bool biometricEnabled})` calling `ApiClient.call('account-settings-update', method: 'PATCH', body: {'biometricEnabled': biometricEnabled})` exactly as in contracts/biometrics-preference-repository.md
- [ ] T016 Create `BiometricsPreferenceRepositoryImpl` implementing `BiometricsPreferenceRepository` in `lib/features/vault/data/account/biometrics_preference_repository_impl.dart` — `save(enabled)` delegates to the remote data source and maps `Right` to `Right(unit)` via `.map((_) {})`, discarding the decoded body (contracts/biometrics-preference-repository.md: "there is no reason to decode and carry the full updated-account payload") — depends on T007, T015
- [ ] T017 [P] Write `BiometricsPreferenceRepositoryImpl` tests in `test/features/vault/data/account/biometrics_preference_repository_impl_test.dart` (mocktail, mocking `ApiClient`, matching `auth_repository_impl_test.dart`'s pattern) covering the 4 scenarios from contracts/biometrics-preference-repository.md: `Right({...})` → `Right(unit)`; `Left(NetworkTimeoutFailure)` passes through unchanged; `Left(NetworkOfflineFailure)` passes through unchanged; `Left(ValidationFailure)` (malformed response) passes through unchanged — depends on T016
- [ ] T018 Register this unit's dependencies in `lib/core/di/service_locator.dart`: `VaultSecureStorage`, `LocalAuthBiometricDataSource`, `VaultRepository` as `registerLazySingleton` (one instance for the app's process lifetime, per contracts/vault-repository.md), `BiometricsPreferenceRemoteDataSource`, `BiometricsPreferenceRepository`, `DetermineVaultEntryUseCase`, and `VaultBloc` as `registerFactory` (matching `AuthBloc`'s registration shape) — depends on T006, T007, T008, T013, T016
- [ ] T019 Create `VaultState` in `lib/features/vault/presentation/bloc/vault_state.dart` — sub-states covering every branch this unit's single bloc must represent: initial/loading, PIN setup (create step, confirm step with mismatch error), biometric prompting, PIN entry (with the optional "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN" error banner and a 4-digit progress-dot count), unlocked

## Dependencies & Execution Order

### Phase Dependencies

- **Setup (Phase 1)**: No dependencies — start immediately.
- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: Depends on Setup (T003 for the route constant) — BLOCKS all user stories.
- **User Stories (Phase 3–6)**: All depend on Foundational completion.
  - US1 and US2 (both P1) should be done first — US2's "biometric fails → PIN" handler extends the
    same `VaultBloc` branch US1's biometric-success handler lives in (T027/T036 both touch
    `vault_bloc.dart`), so doing them in sequence avoids rework, even though each is independently
    testable once done.
  - US3 (P2) extends the same bloc/page with the `pinSetupRequired` branch — independent of US1/US2's
    code paths (different `VaultEntryMode` branch) but shares the file.
  - US4 (P3) only adds a link + navigation handler on top of UI states US1/US2 already built (T028, T037).
- **Polish (Phase 7)**: Depends on all four stories being complete.

### Within Each User Story

- Tests before/alongside implementation (written to fail first, per the template's convention).
- Domain usecases before bloc wiring; bloc wiring before the page UI that reads it.
- Story complete (bloc + page + test) before moving to the next priority.

### Parallel Opportunities

- T002, T003 (Setup) in parallel.
- T004, T005 (entities), T010 (design token), T007 (second repository interface) in parallel within Foundational.
- T009, T014, T017 (test files) can be written in parallel with each other once their respective implementation task lands.
- T025/T026 (US1 usecase + its test) in parallel with T034/T035 (US2 usecase + its test) — different files, both depend only on Foundational.
- T039/T040/T041 (US3 usecases + tests) in parallel with each other.

## Implementation Strategy

### MVP First (User Story 1 Only)

1. Complete Phase 1: Setup.
2. Complete Phase 2: Foundational (CRITICAL — blocks all stories).
3. Complete Phase 3: User Story 1.
4. **STOP and VALIDATE**: cold launch shows the biometric prompt before data; a successful scan
   proceeds; background ≥5 min re-prompts; background <5 min does not. Note that without User
   Story 3, this MVP slice has no PIN ever configured on a fresh device — validate it on a device
   where a PIN already exists (or treat US1+US3 as the realistic minimum demoable slice).

### Incremental Delivery

1. Setup + Foundational → foundation ready (vault route exists, resolves to an empty page).
2. Add US1 → biometric gate works (needs a pre-existing PIN to reach `unlockBiometricFirst`).
3. Add US2 → a failed scan no longer strands the user.
4. Add US3 → a fresh device can actually reach the vault for the first time (PIN now gets created) — this closes the loop US1/US2 needed a PIN for.
5. Add US4 → the "usar e-mail e senha" safety valve.
6. Polish → RNF06/07 gates + quickstart's full manual pass.

Note the real dependency the priorities don't show on their own: **US3 produces the PIN that US1
and US2 require to exist.** Implementing in spec order (US1 → US2 → US3 → US4) is fine for
*writing* the code (Foundational already stubs `hasPinConfigured()`), but *manually demoing* US1/US2
end-to-end needs either a PIN seeded directly via `VaultRepository` in a test, or US3 done first.

# Implementation Plan: P-RF03 — Biometric authentication vault

**Branch**: `002-biometric-auth-vault` (spec directory only — no git branch exists; see spec header)

**Date**: 2026-10-11 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)

**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md`,
`docs/input/requirements.md` §1 (RF03), §10 (parameters), §13 (technical constraints), and
`.specify/memory/constitution.md`. Depends on F000 (`specs/001-foundation/`), already implemented.

## Summary

RF03 inserts a device-local Face ID / Touch ID / PIN barrier between F000's existing session
routing and any screen that shows user data. It adds exactly two new decision points to code F000
already ships — the splash screen's `authenticated` branch and the login/sign-up screen's success
branch — redirecting both from `AppRoutes.home` to a new `AppRoutes.vault` gate instead of adding a
parallel navigation scheme. That single screen (`VaultPage`) internally covers three of the
prototype's named states (Biometria, PIN inicial, PIN após falha) plus first-time PIN
creation, branching on whether a PIN is already configured on the device. A second, independent
mechanism — an app-lifecycle observer feeding a fixed 5-minute domain rule — re-pushes the same
screen over whatever is on screen when the app resumes from a long background period, without
disturbing that screen's state underneath (reusing F000's established `push`-only navigation
discipline, research.md R3). Authentication itself never leaves the device: no biometric data and
no PIN value are ever sent to the backend. The one network call this unit introduces —
persisting the `biometricEnabled` preference via the already-frozen `PATCH /account/settings`
— reuses F000's `ApiClient`/`Either<Failure, T>` path and is fire-and-forget by design (Clarifications).

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: Dart 3.13.4 / Flutter 3.47.5 (stable), pinned via `.fvmrc` — unchanged from
F000, no new pin needed.

**Primary Dependencies** (additions on top of F000's stack):
- `local_auth` — the official Flutter plugin for Face ID/Touch ID; see research.md R1.
- `crypto` — `sha256` hashing of the on-device PIN before it touches secure storage; see research.md R2.
- Reused unchanged from F000: `flutter_bloc`, `fpdart`, `dio` (via `ApiClient`), `get_it`,
  `flutter_secure_storage`, `equatable`, `go_router`; dev-only `mocktail`, `bloc_test`.

**Storage**: `flutter_secure_storage`, extended with two new keys (PIN hash, local biometrics-
preference mirror) via a new `VaultSecureStorage` wrapper parallel to F000's `SecureTokenStorage` —
see data-model.md Device PIN / Biometrics Preference. No SQL/NoSQL local database is introduced.

**Testing**: `flutter_test` + `bloc_test` + `mocktail`, identical to F000; coverage via
`fvm flutter test --coverage`, same `lib/**/domain/**` lcov filter for the RNF07 gate. Device
biometric hardware cannot be exercised by `flutter_test` (no `local_auth` platform channel on the
test VM) — see quickstart.md for the manual iOS Simulator verification steps User Stories 1–2 need.

**Target Platform**: iOS, portrait only — unchanged. `local_auth` requires
`NSFaceIDUsageDescription` in `ios/Runner/Info.plist` (new, see research.md R1); no other native
project change.

**Project Type**: Same single Flutter mobile app; this unit adds one new `lib/features/vault/`
feature folder and touches two existing F000 files at their documented extension points (below).
No backend/server code, no change to `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`.

**Performance Goals**: RNF01 — the biometric prompt itself is OS-rendered (not timed against the
<100 ms/300 ms rule); the one network call this unit makes (`account-settings-update`) shows a
loading indicator only if it exceeds 300 ms, but per FR-014/Clarifications its outcome never blocks
navigation, so in practice no user-visible wait is introduced by this unit at all — PIN
creation/verification and the local biometric prompt are the sum of what stands between the user
and Home/Chat, and both are local.

**Constraints**:
- Authentication is validated entirely on-device (FR-002) — no biometric data or PIN value is ever
  sent to, or checked by, the backend; the backend has no biometric-unlock endpoint by design
  (requirements.md §6.1).
- The 5-minute background timeout is fixed, not user-configurable (FR-009, requirements.md §10).
- No RF01/RF02/RF04–RF10 behavior, no Settings screen, no extension feature (FR-016, FR-017).
- No backend/contract/config change (FR-018) — the only call made is to the already-existing
  `account-settings-update` function, with a request body containing only `biometricEnabled`.
- Clean Architecture, 3 layers per feature (Principle V); domain layer stays free of
  `package:flutter` and `local_auth` types — see contracts/vault-repository.md.
- Zero visual values hardcoded outside `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` (Principle IV/RNF08) — any
  value the vault screens need that isn't already in the token file from F000 is added there, never
  inlined (data-model.md Design Tokens).

**Scale/Scope**: 1 new screen (`VaultPage`, covering Biometria / PIN inicial / PIN após falha / PIN
first-time setup as internal states, per prototype-extract.md's implementation note #1), 1 new
root-level lifecycle observer (no new visible screen — it only decides *when* to push the existing
`VaultPage`), 1 new narrowly-scoped repository (`BiometricsPreferenceRepository`) consuming 1
additional backend operation (`account-settings-update`, `PATCH /account/settings`) beyond F000's
4. Two existing F000 files get a one-line navigation-target change each (`splash_page.dart`,

1	# Data Model: P-RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
2	
3	Source: spec.md §Key Entities, requirements.md §§1, 6.1, 10, prototype-extract.md §§2.1, 3.
4	Entities here are either on-device-only domain objects (Device PIN, Vault Lock State) or a local
5	mirror of one backend field (Biometrics Preference) — this unit introduces no new backend table
6	and no new local database (just two new secure-storage keys alongside F000's four).
7	
8	## Device PIN
9	
10	A 4-digit secret, created once (User Story 3) and checked on every subsequent unlock attempt
11	(User Stories 1–2). Never transmitted to, or validated by, the backend (FR-002).
12	
13	| Field | Type | Notes |
14	|---|---|---|
15	| `pinHash` | `String` (hex, sha256) | Written by `VaultSecureStorage`; see research.md R2 for why the raw digit string is never the thing stored. |
16	
17	**Validation rule**: exactly 4 digits, each `0`–`9`, no partial/shorter value ever written or
18	compared (FR-005). Confirmation during setup is a pure string-equality check between two freshly
19	entered 4-digit values — the first one is held only in memory (`VaultState`) between entry and
20	confirmation, never written to storage until it matches (FR-012: "without the mismatched PIN being
21	saved").
22	
23	## Vault Lock State
24	
25	Whether the current app process currently requires authentication before showing data, and when it
26	was last satisfied — the input to the 5-minute background-resume rule (FR-007–FR-010).
27	
28	| Field | Type | Notes |
29	|---|---|---|
30	| `lastUnlockedAt` | `DateTime?` | In-memory only, held by the `VaultRepository` singleton (one instance for the app's lifetime via `get_it`'s `registerLazySingleton`). `null` until the first successful unlock this process. Never persisted to disk — see research.md R3 for why a killed/relaunched process doesn't need this to survive. |
31	| `backgroundedAt` | `DateTime?` | Set by `VaultLifecycleObserver` on `AppLifecycleState.paused`; read and cleared on the matching `.resumed`. In-memory only, same lifetime as `lastUnlockedAt`. |
32	
33	**Derived decision — `VaultEntryMode`** (domain enum/sealed type, computed by
34	`DetermineVaultEntryUseCase` every time `VaultPage` opens):
35	
36	```
37	pinSetupRequired                      # hasPinConfigured() == false
38	unlockBiometricFirst                  # PIN exists AND biometric capability == available
39	                                       #   AND the local biometrics-preference mirror == true
40	unlockPinOnly                         # PIN exists AND (no biometric capability OR preference == false)
41	```
42	
43	**State transitions**:
44	
45	```
46	[SplashPage, SessionStatusAuthenticated]  or  [LoginSignupPage, AuthStatus.authenticated (non-reauth)]
47	  context.push(AppRoutes.vault)   # mode: gatekeeper
48	      VaultPage opens -> DetermineVaultEntryUseCase()
49	          pinSetupRequired      -> show "Digite seu PIN" (new) -> confirm -> [optional] offer biometrics
50	                                     -> on complete: markUnlocked() -> context.go(AppRoutes.home)     (Story 3)
51	          unlockBiometricFirst  -> auto-trigger local_auth prompt
52	              success                     -> markUnlocked() -> context.go(AppRoutes.home)   (Story 1)
53	              failed/cancelled/notAvailable -> show "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN" + PIN keypad (Story 2;
54	                                                notAvailable routed identically — e.g. biometric lockout mid-session)
55	                  correct PIN      -> markUnlocked() -> context.go(AppRoutes.home)
56	                  incorrect PIN    -> clear digits, keep error banner, no lockout, retry allowed (Story 2, Edge Cases)
57	          unlockPinOnly          -> show PIN keypad directly, no biometric prompt attempted (Edge Cases: no hardware/not enrolled/OS-disabled)
58	      at any point: "usar e-mail e senha" -> context.push(AppRoutes.login)          (Story 4)
59	
60	[VaultLifecycleObserver, AppLifecycleState.resumed, EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase() == true]
61	  rootNavigatorKey.push(VaultPage)   # mode: relock — pushed OVER whatever screen is current
62	      VaultPage opens -> DetermineVaultEntryUseCase()   # always unlockBiometricFirst or unlockPinOnly — PIN already exists
63	          success (biometric or PIN)  -> markUnlocked() -> Navigator.pop()   # reveals the preserved screen underneath, state untouched
64	
65	[VaultLifecycleObserver, AppLifecycleState.resumed, EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase() == false]
66	  no-op — screen underneath was never covered, no re-authentication required   (FR-008)
67	```
68	
69	**Fixed rule** (`EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase`, FR-009):
70	
71	```dart
72	bool call({required DateTime? backgroundedAt, required DateTime resumedAt}) {
73	  if (backgroundedAt == null) return false;
74	  return resumedAt.difference(backgroundedAt) >= const Duration(minutes: 5);
75	}
76	```
77	
78	A pure function of two timestamps and one constant — no settings read, no parameter — is itself
79	the mechanism by which FR-009's "fixed value, not configurable by the user" is enforced.
80	
81	## Biometrics Preference
82	
83	An account-level flag indicating whether Face ID/Touch ID is the user's chosen unlock method —
84	read locally at every vault entry to decide `unlockBiometricFirst` vs. `unlockPinOnly`, and mirrored
85	to the backend for durability/future display (RF09's Settings screen), per FR-013.
86	
87	| Field | Type | Notes |
88	|---|---|---|
89	| `biometricPreferenceLocal` | `bool` | Written to `VaultSecureStorage` during first-time PIN setup (Story 3, scenario 4) if the user opts in; this is the value `DetermineVaultEntryUseCase` actually reads at runtime — never the backend's copy (research.md R6). Defaults to `false` until set. |
90	| `biometricEnabled` (remote) | `bool` | The backend's `users.biometric_enabled` field (requirements.md §8), read/written only through `PATCH /account/settings` → `account-settings-update`. This unit only ever **writes** it (fire-and-forget, FR-014); it never reads it back. |
91	
92	**Write path** (`SaveBiometricsPreferenceUseCase`, FR-013/FR-014):
93	
94	```
95	1. VaultRepository.setBiometricPreferenceLocally(enabled)        # synchronous, always succeeds (local write)
96	2. BiometricsPreferenceRepository.save(enabled)                  # await, discard Either<Failure, T> result
97	3. proceed to Home/Chat regardless of step 2's outcome            # Clarifications; Edge Cases
98	```
99	
100	## Backend Failure (reused, not redefined)
101	
102	`BiometricsPreferenceRepository.save()` is the only network call this unit makes; it returns
103	`Either<Failure, T>` using F000's existing `core/network/failure.dart` hierarchy unchanged (no new
104	`Failure` subtype — research.md R5). The three scenarios covered by this unit's own tests, toward
105	RNF09's 15-scenario total:
106	
107	| Scenario | Expected `Failure` | `retryable` |
108	|---|---|---|
109	| Request exceeds the timeout | `NetworkTimeoutFailure` | yes |
110	| No connection at all | `NetworkOfflineFailure` | yes |
111	| Malformed response body | `ValidationFailure` | no |
112

114	unit's own `mocktail` tests of `BiometricsPreferenceRepositoryImpl`, never surfaced to the user.
115	
116	## Biometric Capability (domain enum, no `local_auth` type crosses into `domain/`)
117	
118	```
119	available        # canCheckBiometrics && isDeviceSupported && getAvailableBiometrics().isNotEmpty
120	noHardware        # isDeviceSupported == false
121	notEnrolled        # hardware present, nothing enrolled at the OS level
122	osDisabled        # was available in a previous session, no longer (Edge Cases: OS-level disable between sessions)
123	```
124	
125	`LocalAuthBiometricDataSource` (data layer) is the only place that imports `local_auth`'s own
126	types (`LocalAuthentication`, `AuthenticationOptions`, `BiometricType`); `VaultRepositoryImpl` maps
127	its result into this enum before it ever reaches `domain/` or `presentation/` (RNF06).

130	
131	- **`VaultMode`** (`gatekeeper | relock`) — which of the two entry points opened `VaultPage`;
132	  decides `go(home)` vs. `pop()` on success (data-model.md State transitions above). Passed as a

# Data Model: P-RF03 — Biometric authentication vault

Source: spec.md §Key Entities, requirements.md §§1, 6.1, 10, prototype-extract.md §§2.1, 3.
Entities here are either on-device-only domain objects (Device PIN, Vault Lock State) or a local
mirror of one backend field (Biometrics Preference) — this unit introduces no new backend table
and no new local database (just two new secure-storage keys alongside F000's four).

## Device PIN

A 4-digit secret, created once (User Story 3) and checked on every subsequent unlock attempt
(User Stories 1–2). Never transmitted to, or validated by, the backend (FR-002).

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `pinHash` | `String` (hex, sha256) | Written by `VaultSecureStorage`; see research.md R2 for why the raw digit string is never the thing stored. |

**Validation rule**: exactly 4 digits, each `0`–`9`, no partial/shorter value ever written or
compared (FR-005). Confirmation during setup is a pure string-equality check between two freshly
entered 4-digit values — the first one is held only in memory (`VaultState`) between entry and
confirmation, never written to storage until it matches (FR-012: "without the mismatched PIN being
saved").

## Vault Lock State

Whether the current app process currently requires authentication before showing data, and when it
was last satisfied — the input to the 5-minute background-resume rule (FR-007–FR-010).

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `lastUnlockedAt` | `DateTime?` | In-memory only, held by the `VaultRepository` singleton (one instance for the app's lifetime via `get_it`'s `registerLazySingleton`). `null` until the first successful unlock this process. Never persisted to disk — see research.md R3 for why a killed/relaunched process doesn't need this to survive. |
| `backgroundedAt` | `DateTime?` | Set by `VaultLifecycleObserver` on `AppLifecycleState.paused`; read and cleared on the matching `.resumed`. In-memory only, same lifetime as `lastUnlockedAt`. |

**Derived decision — `VaultEntryMode`** (domain enum/sealed type, computed by
`DetermineVaultEntryUseCase` every time `VaultPage` opens):

```
pinSetupRequired                      # hasPinConfigured() == false
unlockBiometricFirst                  # PIN exists AND biometric capability == available
                                       #   AND the local biometrics-preference mirror == true
unlockPinOnly                         # PIN exists AND (no biometric capability OR preference == false)
```

**State transitions**:

```
[SplashPage, SessionStatusAuthenticated]  or  [LoginSignupPage, AuthStatus.authenticated (non-reauth)]
  context.push(AppRoutes.vault)   # mode: gatekeeper
      VaultPage opens -> DetermineVaultEntryUseCase()
          pinSetupRequired      -> show "Digite seu PIN" (new) -> confirm -> [optional] offer biometrics
                                     -> on complete: markUnlocked() -> context.go(AppRoutes.home)     (Story 3)
          unlockBiometricFirst  -> auto-trigger local_auth prompt
              success                     -> markUnlocked() -> context.go(AppRoutes.home)   (Story 1)
              failed/cancelled/notAvailable -> show "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN" + PIN keypad (Story 2;
                                                notAvailable routed identically — e.g. biometric lockout mid-session)
                  correct PIN      -> markUnlocked() -> context.go(AppRoutes.home)
                  incorrect PIN    -> clear digits, keep error banner, no lockout, retry allowed (Story 2, Edge Cases)
          unlockPinOnly          -> show PIN keypad directly, no biometric prompt attempted (Edge Cases: no hardware/not enrolled/OS-disabled)
      at any point: "usar e-mail e senha" -> context.push(AppRoutes.login)          (Story 4)

[VaultLifecycleObserver, AppLifecycleState.resumed, EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase() == true]
  rootNavigatorKey.push(VaultPage)   # mode: relock — pushed OVER whatever screen is current
      VaultPage opens -> DetermineVaultEntryUseCase()   # always unlockBiometricFirst or unlockPinOnly — PIN already exists
          success (biometric or PIN)  -> markUnlocked() -> Navigator.pop()   # reveals the preserved screen underneath, state untouched

[VaultLifecycleObserver, AppLifecycleState.resumed, EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase() == false]
  no-op — screen underneath was never covered, no re-authentication required   (FR-008)
```

**Fixed rule** (`EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase`, FR-009):

```dart
bool call({required DateTime? backgroundedAt, required DateTime resumedAt}) {
  if (backgroundedAt == null) return false;
  return resumedAt.difference(backgroundedAt) >= const Duration(minutes: 5);
}
```

A pure function of two timestamps and one constant — no settings read, no parameter — is itself
the mechanism by which FR-009's "fixed value, not configurable by the user" is enforced.

## Biometrics Preference

An account-level flag indicating whether Face ID/Touch ID is the user's chosen unlock method —
read locally at every vault entry to decide `unlockBiometricFirst` vs. `unlockPinOnly`, and mirrored
to the backend for durability/future display (RF09's Settings screen), per FR-013.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `biometricPreferenceLocal` | `bool` | Written to `VaultSecureStorage` during first-time PIN setup (Story 3, scenario 4) if the user opts in; this is the value `DetermineVaultEntryUseCase` actually reads at runtime — never the backend's copy (research.md R6). Defaults to `false` until set. |
| `biometricEnabled` (remote) | `bool` | The backend's `users.biometric_enabled` field (requirements.md §8), read/written only through `PATCH /account/settings` → `account-settings-update`. This unit only ever **writes** it (fire-and-forget, FR-014); it never reads it back. |

**Write path** (`SaveBiometricsPreferenceUseCase`, FR-013/FR-014):

```
1. VaultRepository.setBiometricPreferenceLocally(enabled)        # synchronous, always succeeds (local write)
2. BiometricsPreferenceRepository.save(enabled)                  # await, discard Either<Failure, T> result
3. proceed to Home/Chat regardless of step 2's outcome            # Clarifications; Edge Cases
```

## Backend Failure (reused, not redefined)

`BiometricsPreferenceRepository.save()` is the only network call this unit makes; it returns
`Either<Failure, T>` using F000's existing `core/network/failure.dart` hierarchy unchanged (no new
`Failure` subtype — research.md R5). The three scenarios covered by this unit's own tests, toward
RNF09's 15-scenario total:

| Scenario | Expected `Failure` | `retryable` |
|---|---|---|
| Request exceeds the timeout | `NetworkTimeoutFailure` | yes |
| No connection at all | `NetworkOfflineFailure` | yes |
| Malformed response body | `ValidationFailure` | no |

None of these three block the PIN-setup-complete transition (R6) — they are observed only by this
unit's own `mocktail` tests of `BiometricsPreferenceRepositoryImpl`, never surfaced to the user.

## Biometric Capability (domain enum, no `local_auth` type crosses into `domain/`)

```
available        # canCheckBiometrics && isDeviceSupported && getAvailableBiometrics().isNotEmpty
noHardware        # isDeviceSupported == false
notEnrolled        # hardware present, nothing enrolled at the OS level
osDisabled        # was available in a previous session, no longer (Edge Cases: OS-level disable between sessions)
```

`LocalAuthBiometricDataSource` (data layer) is the only place that imports `local_auth`'s own
types (`LocalAuthentication`, `AuthenticationOptions`, `BiometricType`); `VaultRepositoryImpl` maps
its result into this enum before it ever reaches `domain/` or `presentation/` (RNF06).

## Presentation-only state (not persisted, not a domain entity)

- **`VaultMode`** (`gatekeeper | relock`) — which of the two entry points opened `VaultPage`;
  decides `go(home)` vs. `pop()` on success (data-model.md State transitions above). Passed as a
  constructor parameter, not stored anywhere.
- **First-entry PIN held during confirmation** — the first 4-digit value typed during first-time
  setup, kept only in `VaultBloc`'s in-memory state until the confirmation entry either matches
  (written to storage) or doesn't (discarded, user restarts entry — FR-012).
- **PIN-entry digit buffer / progress-dot count** — transient widget/bloc state for the keypad,
  reset to empty after every failed attempt (Edge Cases: "the entered digits are cleared").

## Design Tokens (`lib/core/design_tokens.dart`) — additions only

Every color, type style, spacing, and radius the vault screens use already exists from F000
(`colorPrimary`, `colorOnPrimary`, `colorError`, `colorSurfaceBg`, `textHeadlineMd`, `textBodyMd`,
`textTitleSm`, `spacing*`, `radius*`). One value is new, per research.md R7:

| Token | Value | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `sizeKeypadTapTarget` | `72` (double, dp) | `pin_keypad.dart` — the circular tap target for each of the 12 keys (digits 0–9 + backspace + the empty 4th-row-left cell), per the prototype's "3×4 numeric keypad" with no explicit pixel size given. |

No other component-level token (spine colors, sync badge, bookmark states, etc.) is needed — those
belong to later units' own screens, same precedent F000's data-model.md already set.

1	# Research: P-RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
2	
3	F000's research.md explicitly left "biometrics" open for "the units that need them (RF03, RF09)."
4	This file resolves that, plus every other free choice and silent spot this unit's spec surfaces.
5	
6	## R1 — Biometrics package
7	
8	- **Decision**: `local_auth` (the official `flutter.dev`-maintained plugin), called with
9	  `authenticate(biometricOnly: true)`.
10	- **Rationale**: FR-004 requires that a failed/unavailable biometric attempt fall through to the
11	  app's **own** 4-digit PIN, never to the iOS device passcode. `local_auth`'s `biometricOnly: true`
12	  option is honored on iOS (it pins the underlying `LAPolicy` to
13	  `LAPolicyDeviceOwnerAuthenticationWithBiometrics`, which has no device-passcode fallback built
14	  in) — exactly the primitive FR-004 needs. `local_auth` also exposes `canCheckBiometrics` and
15	  `isDeviceSupported()` ahead of calling `authenticate`, which FR-003 and the Edge Cases ("no
16	  hardware," "nothing enrolled," "disabled at the OS level") need to distinguish from an in-progress
17	  failed attempt. It is the only Flutter-ecosystem plugin maintained by the Flutter team itself for
18	  this exact purpose, consistent with picking boring, well-supported dependencies for a stack the
19	  constitution otherwise keeps deliberately small.
20	- **Alternatives considered**: Rolling a native iOS `LAContext` call through a hand-written
21	  platform channel — rejected, `local_auth` already wraps exactly this with no extra capability
22	  gained from going lower-level, for meaningfully more code to own and test. Third-party biometrics
23	  wrappers (e.g. ones that bundle PIN-entry UI too) — rejected, this unit already owns PIN entry per
24	  FR-005/the prototype's exact keypad spec, and a bundled UI would fight Principle IV (design-token
25	  fidelity) rather than help.
26	- **Native project note**: `local_auth`'s iOS backend requires `NSFaceIDUsageDescription` in
27	  `ios/Runner/Info.plist` (a one-line string the App Store requires before Face ID can even be
28	  attempted) — the only native project file this unit touches, and a hard requirement of the
29	  package rather than a product decision. No Android work exists in this project (iOS-only,
30	  Principle II).
31	
32	## R2 — PIN storage
33	
34	- **Decision**: Store `sha256(pin)` (hex string) via a new `VaultSecureStorage` key, never the raw
35	  4-digit value. Verification re-hashes the entered PIN and compares digests.
36	- **Rationale**: `flutter_secure_storage` is already Keychain-backed (R5 of F000's research.md),
37	  so storing the raw PIN would not be *readable* in plaintext at rest either — but hashing is the
38	  standard defense-in-depth for any credential-shaped value regardless of the storage layer
39	  underneath, and it is a one-function addition (`crypto`'s `sha256`) with no behavioral
40	  downside: the PIN is never displayed back to the user, so there is no legitimate need to ever
41	  recover the raw value, only to compare it. This mirrors how the backend itself never stores or
42	  sees passwords in the clear.
43	- **Alternatives considered**: Storing the raw PIN string — rejected as an avoidable weakening for
44	  zero functional gain. A salted hash (per-install random salt, also stored) — rejected as
45	  over-engineering: the threat a salt defends against is an attacker who has compromised *many*
46	  users' hash stores at once and wants to precompute one rainbow table across all of them; here,
47	  each hash lives alone inside that one device's own encrypted Keychain entry for that one user, so
48	  a salt adds code and a second stored value without changing what an attacker who already has
49	  Keychain access could do.
50	
51	## R3 — Where the 5-minute relock timer lives
52	
53	- **Decision**: One root-level `StatefulWidget` (`VaultLifecycleObserver`), installed once in
54	  `main.dart`'s `CerneApp.builder` (the same spot F000 installs the session-expired
55	  `BlocListener`), implementing `WidgetsBindingObserver`. On `AppLifecycleState.paused` it calls
56	  into the long-lived `VaultRepository` singleton to record "now"; on `.resumed` it asks a pure
57	  domain usecase (`EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase`) whether that gap was ≥ 5 minutes, and if so
58	  pushes `VaultPage(mode: relock)` via the existing `rootNavigatorKey` — the same root navigator
59	  `session_expired_overlay.dart` already pushes onto.
60	- **Rationale**: FR-007/FR-008/FR-010 and User Story 1's background-resume scenarios are a
61	  cross-cutting concern that has nothing to do with *which* screen happens to be on top — exactly
62	  the shape F000's own `SessionBloc` + root `BlocListener` pattern was built for (research.md R3
63	  there). Reusing `rootNavigatorKey` and plain `push` (never `go`/replace) is what makes "the screen
64	  underneath keeps its exact state" (FR-010) true by construction, not by a second bespoke
65	  mechanism — the same guarantee `session_expired_overlay.dart` already relies on for its own
66	  overlay.
67	- **Why not persist the last-unlock timestamp to disk**: the only case that would matter for is the
68	  OS killing the process while backgrounded — but that case is *already* handled for free: a killed
69	  process means the next launch is a cold launch, which always re-enters `SplashPage` → the
70	  `AppRoutes.vault` gatekeeper path regardless of elapsed time (Edge Cases: "the next launch is
71	  treated as a cold launch and always shows the vault"). An in-memory timestamp on a singleton
72	  repository is therefore sufficient; persisting it would add a disk write on every background
73	  transition for a case that can't be reached.
74	- **Alternatives considered**: A second root-level `Bloc` dedicated to lock state — rejected as an
75	  unnecessary extra moving part; the logic needed (record a timestamp, compare it, decide whether
76	  to push one specific, already-existing route) does not need its own event/state machine distinct
77	  from the domain usecase plus a thin observer widget. A `Timer.periodic` ticking down from 5
78	  minutes while foregrounded — rejected: FR-007/FR-008 only care about elapsed *background* time,
79	  not foreground idle time (that is RF08's unrelated 2-minute inactivity trigger), so a running
80	  foreground timer would be solving a problem this requirement doesn't have.
81	
82	## R4 — The single-screen vault (gatekeeper vs. relock, setup vs. unlock)
83	
84	- **Decision**: One route (`AppRoutes.vault`), one page (`VaultPage`), one screen-scoped
85	  `VaultBloc`, branching internally on two independent axes: (a) **mode** — `gatekeeper` (reached
86	  from `SplashPage` or `LoginSignupPage`, resolves by going to `AppRoutes.home` on success) vs.
87	  `relock` (reached from `VaultLifecycleObserver`, resolves by popping back to the preserved screen
88	  underneath); (b) **entry decision** — `pinSetupRequired` vs. `locked(biometricFirst | pinOnly)`,
89	  computed once by `DetermineVaultEntryUseCase` when the page opens.
90	- **Rationale**: prototype-extract.md's own implementation note #1 flags that "32 states" collapse
91	  into fewer real screens with internal state, naming this exact family (Biometria / PIN inicial /
92	  PIN após falha) as a candidate. The spec's own Assumptions go further and fold first-time PIN
93	  creation into the same keypad component rather than inventing a fourth undocumented screen. A
94	  `relock` entry can never need the `pinSetupRequired` branch (a relock is only ever triggered after
95	  the app was already unlocked once this process, which requires a PIN to already exist) — so the
96	  same `DetermineVaultEntryUseCase` naturally degrades to just the unlock branch for that mode
97	  without needing a second decision function.
98	- **Alternatives considered**: Four separate routes (one per prototype state name) — rejected,
99	  directly contradicts the prototype's own implementation note and would duplicate the keypad
100	  widget and its 350 ms-after-4th-digit transition behavior four times instead of once.
101	
102	## R5 — RNF09 scoping for this unit's local-only operations
103	
104	- **Decision**: `Either<Failure, T>` is used only where this unit actually talks to the network —
105	  `BiometricsPreferenceRepository`. `VaultRepository` (PIN verification, biometric hardware
106	  queries, the in-memory relock timestamp) returns plain `bool`/`DateTime?`/domain-enum values, not
107	  `Either<Failure, T>`.
108	- **Rationale**: RNF09's `Failure` hierarchy (`core/network/failure.dart`) is explicitly the
109	  backend's own closed 13-code taxonomy (F000 research.md R6) — `AUTH_EXPIRED`,
110	  `NETWORK_TIMEOUT`, and so on are all things *a server response* can say. A missing fingerprint
111	  sensor or a wrong PIN digest is not a server outcome and has no corresponding code; forcing it
112	  through `Either<Failure, T>` would mean either inventing fake codes for purely local conditions
113	  (polluting a taxonomy the spec calls "closed") or always returning a code that doesn't really fit.
114	  Constitution Principle I directs implementers to make the reasonable call where the inputs are
115	  silent, and RNF09's own wording ("every repository") is about the network-error-handling pattern
116	  the requirement is named for — not a blanket ban on any repository ever returning something else
117	  for a condition that isn't a network failure.
118	- **Alternatives considered**: Modeling PIN/biometric outcomes as `Either<Failure, T>` with new
119	  `Failure` subtypes (e.g. `BiometricUnavailableFailure`) — rejected: it would grow the "closed"
120	  taxonomy with codes the backend's `error-taxonomy.md` doesn't define and that no later unit's
